Chāṅgu Nārāyaṇa

    Inscription in front of the
    Changu Nārāyaṇa Temple. A slab of stone in front of the western gate of the temple of
    Changu Nārāyaṇa near the victory pillar of Mānadeva and behind the image of Garuḍa.
    The top of the stone shows a vessel bearing a bunch of flowers at the centre and on two
    sides a decorative design of flowers in full bloom, all in relief. Date illegible because
    of the last line being damaged. The inscribed part is 46 cm wide and 62 cm long. The
    inscription belongs to the reign of śivadeva I. (R).
    Bhaṭṭāraka Mahārāja śrī śivadeva from Mānagriha. On the advice (vijñāpitena) of
    śrī Sāmanta Aṃśuvarman; sarvva-koṭṭa-maryyād-opapannatvād;
    śilāpaṭṭaka-śāsanam-idaṃ vo dattam. Records the second stage of grant (not marked
    as prasāda) a village Guṃdīmaka, granted formerly, accordingly the koṭṭa rules. With
    other grants of land (? Dakṣiṇa-rāja-kula-puṇḍi-rāja-kulayor-bhūmi-kṣettraiḥ) and
